messages:
lina_support: Hey team — ACME says some requests are getting 401s and we can't see request IDs in their screenshots. Can someone sketch a tiny ask/checklist I can send them so we get a repro + trace?

raj_engineer: Quick checklist idea: ask for (1) the raw HTTP request/response headers (copy-paste), (2) a curl they ran (or a HAR), (3) the Debug Token from our Console, and (4) exact ISO timestamp of the failing request and region. Short and actionable.

lina_support: Perfect. I'll ping them. How do we tell them where the Debug Token lives in the UI now? UI path was tweaked.

raj_engineer: Updated path: Console -> Debug -> Sessions -> click the row -> Copy debug token. Tell them to paste the whole token string (starts with dt_).

emma_sre: Add: request the x-rw-request-id or x-request-id from the response headers if present, and ask whether there's an edge proxy / CDN in front that might strip headers. If latency is involved, ask for approximate p95/p99 and whether they saw timeouts.

lina_support: Copying into message to ACME: "Please attach either a HAR or run the curl below from the same environment where the error happened and paste stderr. Also include the Debug Token (Console → Debug → Sessions → Copy debug token), the exact ISO timestamp of the failing request, and any proxy/CDN details."

raj_engineer: Here's a tiny curl snippet you can paste: 

```
curl -v \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <YOUR_API_KEY>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "x-rw-trace: 1" \
  --data '{"input":"test repro"}' \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
```

Tell them to replace <YOUR_API_KEY> and paste the full terminal output (both stdout and stderr). The `-v` shows headers so we can see request/response ids.

emma_sre: For SDK cases, ask them to paste the last 10 lines of their SDK logs and specifically look for `session_ref`, `reqref`, or `x-rw-request-id`. Example log lines: `info: sent request session_ref=abc123 reqref=xyz789 status=401`. That makes tracing trivial.

lina_support: Good note — I'll ask them to search client logs for those keys. Also should we ask for the token TTL/refresh flow when it's auth related?

raj_engineer: Yes — short question: "Are you using a short-lived token or a static key? If short-lived, include the exact clock skew (client time vs UTC) or steps to reproduce the auth flow."

lina_support: Sending ACME now. I'll include both the curl snippet and the console path, plus ask them to attach a HAR if they can.

debug-bot: New debug token created for account acme-corp: dt_redacted (token redacted in-channel).

emma_sre: When you escalate to Eng, include: 1) debug token, 2) the timestamp, 3) the x-rw-request-id (or session_ref), 4) the curl/HAR, and 5) any proxy headers. In Eng logs look for the request id and then check routing decisions and auth plugin logs.

lina_support: Thanks — I'll bundle and tag @oncall-eng if ACME can't reproduce. Short, clear thread — great.

raj_engineer: :thumbsup: For the handoff snippet to paste into a ticket/eng slack: 
- debug_token: dt_<redacted>
- timestamp (ISO): 2025-09-15T14:32:10Z
- region: us-west-2
- sample curl/HAR attached
- observed response headers (copy)

That gets Eng immediate lookup.

lina_support: Solid. Closing this thread after ACME attaches files.

emma_sre: One last tip: if they provide only a browser HAR, also ask them to run the curl once to rule out client-side transform. Browser extensions sometimes rewrite headers.
